sphere_commentary.overview:
Mean efficacy is consistent across HEALING and THRIVING (6.96–6.98), with TRANSFORMING trailing at 6.59 — consistent with its ascending-arc design targeting lower-affect listeners.
• HEALING leads in sample size (n=574) and consistency, with strongest signal in H-OS-L1 (n=95, mean 7.15).
• THRIVING peaks at T-FC-L3 (mean 7.63), the highest single-protocol observed mean in the set.
• TRANSFORMING carries widest variance and largest AutoGluon–observed gaps, particularly for X-ME-L1 and X-MD-L1.
sphere_commentary.cross_series:
Series profiles align with their design intent — HEALING for regulation, THRIVING for cognitive optimisation, TRANSFORMING for ascending-arc low-affect entry.
• HEALING shows highest n and tightest consistency; H-CR-* sits lower as structurally expected given crisis entry states.
• THRIVING peaks in Focus & Clarity at T-FC-L3 (7.63), with T-CF-L3 also elevated (7.28) at developing confidence.
• TRANSFORMING shows widest spread and largest AutoGluon–observed gaps (X-ME-L1, X-MD-L1, X-MC-L3) — panel divided on whether this reflects model blind spot or genuine listener-state variance.
sphere_commentary.anomalies:
Several protocols show meaningful divergence between AutoGluon ensemble predictions and observed outcomes, suggesting captured entrainment dynamics not fully reflected in the model.
• X-ME-L1: AutoGluon predicts 8.23 vs observed 6.74 — largest single gap (1.49), warrants entrainment-delay investigation.
• H-CR-L2: AutoGluon predicts 7.96 vs observed 6.52 — model overestimates crisis efficacy by 1.44; possible model blind spot for acute-distress entry states.
• X-MC-L3: lowest mean (5.70) with highest std (2.45) and n=10 — bimodal flag, but early data; do not over-interpret.
• YouTube retention data is entirely absent across all protocols — reach signals exist but engagement cannot be evaluated.
sphere_commentary.development_signals:
Convergent signals were raised independently by multiple analyzers; these carry the most weight and are prefixed below.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] X-ME-L1 (n=39) — investigate entrainment delay and rhythm architecture; largest AutoGluon–observed gap in the library.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] H-CR-L2 (n=33) — crisis efficacy below model expectation; investigate model blind spot and Adviser routing for acute-distress listeners.
• [CONVERGENT SIGNAL] T-FC-L3 (n=35) — highest in THRIVING (7.63); consider L4 variant and increased adviser routing.
• X-MC-L3 (n=10) — create an alternative Hz exploration or L2 variant given low mean and high variance; low confidence, treat as early signal.
• H-SL-L2 (n=45) — 3 of 15 rate rhythm 'too busy' on a descent protocol; evaluate hold-phase reduction or rhythm simplification.
• T-FC-L1 (n=41) — 9 of 23 rate rhythm 'slightly busy' on a hold protocol; consider holding tighter rhythmic density for this level.
sphere_commentary.embedding_analysis:
Cross-run drift is substantial across nearly all protocols, suggesting either evolving analytical framing or genuine signal shifts; cluster analysis is unavailable due to data sparsity.
• CROSS-RUN DRIFT: 15+ protocols show similarity below 0.70, with X-MD-L3 (0.507), H-SL-L1 (0.530), and T-FC-L3 (0.532) lowest.
• CROSS-PROTOCOL SEMANTIC CLUSTERS: insufficient protocols with embeddings for cluster analysis — note only.
• Confidence note: drift is widespread rather than isolated; treat individual protocol narratives as developing interpretations subject to revision.

by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L1: Many people find this helps with anxiety, with effects building over the first ten minutes. One of the most consistently calming options in the set.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L2: A steady option for stress, often used during therapy or commuting. Most people settle into it within five minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-AX-L3: Works well for some listeners, though not clearly better than earlier levels. Some take longer to settle into the longer arc.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L1: Used in difficult moments, with some reporting real relief. Lower scores are expected — listeners arrive in extreme states.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L2: Slightly better than H-CR-L1 for many, though feedback is mixed. Some love it, others find it unremarkable.
by_protocol_plain.H-CR-L3: Can help quickly for some, but a small number say it worsened things. Best treated as a fast-acting grounding option, not universally calming.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L1: One of the most popular and well-loved protocols for overstimulation. Most people notice a difference within about ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L2: Works reliably for overwhelm, though not everyone connects with the music. Most settle in around ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.H-OS-L3: Helps people wind down, especially before sleep. Feedback is positive, though slightly less strong than the earlier levels.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L1: A top choice for sleep, with many feeling its effect quickly. The data suggests room for it to be even more effective.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L2: Used a lot by caregivers, but some find the rhythm too active for sleep. Takes a little longer to settle into than expected.
by_protocol_plain.H-SL-L3: Helps some people relax, but a few didn't settle at all. A quieter presence, though not a consistent sleep aid yet.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L1: Only mildly helpful for most people in creative flow. Some feel a slight lift, but many don't notice much change.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L2: A little better than L1 for some, especially those needing gentle focus. A few listeners love it, but it's not widely used.
by_protocol_plain.T-CF-L3: Shows real promise for deep flow, with some reporting strong gains. Still early data, but the signal is encouraging.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L1: Mixed experience — some find real clarity, others feel the rhythm is slightly busy. Works better for some than others.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L2: More effective than L1 for focus, often used in therapy or caregiving. Takes about ten minutes to feel the effects.
by_protocol_plain.T-FC-L3: One of the most powerful protocols in the set for focus, with many reporting genuine improvement. A standout.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L1: Balanced and steady, but slow to take effect for some. Works best when you have time for the full session.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L2: Results vary — some like it, others find the rhythm too busy. Most settle in around five to ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.T-MB-L3: Helps some maintain balance, but a few didn't settle at all. Still needs more testing at this level.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L1: Most notice a benefit for clearer thinking, though a small number had negative reactions. Settles in about ten minutes.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L2: Fast-acting for some, with strong clarity effects. One of the better performers in its category.
by_protocol_plain.X-MC-L3: Less consistent — some find it too busy and don't settle. Still early data, so treat this as a developing signal.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L1: Helps some with motivation, especially within the first five minutes. Results vary widely from person to person.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L2: A gentle lift for some, with a few listeners loving the music. Takes longer to settle into than expected.
by_protocol_plain.X-MD-L3: Strong outcomes for some listeners, but the experience varies a lot. Still early — interpret with care.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L1: A good mood booster for many, and the data suggests it has more potential than current usage reveals. Worth investigating.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L2: Lifts mood nicely for many, with some settling immediately and others needing more time. A mixed but positive signal.
by_protocol_plain.X-ME-L3: Helps some with energy, though results are inconsistent across listeners. Still early data — developing signal.
